item.title: Congo Gold Finances IS-Backed Rebels Through Uganda, Sentry Says
item.description: The Islamic State-backed Allied Democratic Forces is financing itself through gold mined in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo exported through Uganda, according to a report by The Sentry.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Kavanagh

item.title: South Africa Deploys Troops in Restive Province Before Elections
item.description: South Africa will deploy troops in KwaZulu-Natal to ensure security in a province that has witnessed incidents of anti-immigrant violence, as the country prepares for municipal elections next week.
item.dc:creator: Alister Bull

item.title: Burnham Helps Labour to a Large Poll Bounce to Mark 100th Day
item.description: When he first became prime minister, Andy Burnham’s Conservative opponents labeled him a “people pleaser.”
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid

item.title: Finland and Norway Hold ‘Frank’ Call With Putin on Ukraine
item.description: Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the prospects for a peace deal in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Trade AI and Oil, Not Policy or Politics: Market Analysis
item.description: Guy Johnson, Oliver Crook and Mark Cudmore break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Mega IPO Filing Renews AI Trade Optimism
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Global stocks advanced as Anthropic's filing for an initial public offering renewed optimism over the artificial intelligence trade following recent strains.
HSBC shares slumped in Hong Kong after the bank posted earnings that fell short of estimates in the third quarter and kept its outlook for the rest of year unchanged.
And Israel is holding its first election since the 2023 Hamas attack, a vote many consider to be the country’s most consequential in decades.
Today guest: Verena Ross, European Securities and Markets Authority Chair. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Melania Trump-Backed Local Truce Begins in Ukrainian Town
item.description: Russia and Ukraine halted fighting around Oleshky, a war-ravaged town in the Russian-controlled part of southern Ukraine, under a rare local ceasefire brokered with the involvement of US First Lady Melania Trump.
item.dc:creator: Aliaksandr Kudrytski

item.title: Merz Pitches Closer EU-Asia Ties, Warns of China Pressure
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Asia can benefit from closer ties across trade and security issues as both regions face pressures from great powers, particularly China.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dahinten and Michael Nienaber

item.title: Israelis Go to Polls as Netanyahu Seeks Reelection
item.description: Israel is holding its first election since the 2023 Hamas attack in a vote many consider to be the country’s most consequential in decades. Polls have consistently forecast a razor-thin outcome as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks reelection and his opponents, led by former armed forces chief Gadi Eisenkot, call him Israel's greatest threat. Bloomberg's Dan Williams reports from Jerusalem. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sutcliffe: Saudis in Tehran on Iran War, Houthi Conflict
item.description: Oil pulled back as a fresh diplomatic push raised hopes of avoiding another escalation in the US-Iran conflict. Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iran's leadership in Tehran, with both sides agreeing to continue discussions ahead of the US midterms and Israel elections. Megan Sutcliffe, Principal Analyst Middle East & Africa at Sybilline spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa on significance of the meeting. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israelis Go to Polls in Tight Race to Decide Netanyahu’s Fate
item.description: Israel is holding its first election since the 2023 Hamas attack that traumatized the nation and triggered the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, a vote many consider to be the country’s most consequential in decades.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Bronner

item.title: What John Healey Plans in the First Budget of Andy Burnham’s UK Premiership
item.description: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will deliver his first budget on Wednesday in a key test for Andy Burnham’s new Labour administration as it seeks to maintain a bounce in the polls and keep investors on side.
item.dc:creator: Joe Mayes

item.title: Trump Says Golf Course Project Will Proceed Despite Court Order
item.description: President Donald Trump vowed to appeal a federal judge’s order to restrict his sweeping plan to transform a municipal golf course in Washington into a championship course.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: Singapore’s Top Envoy Visits Indonesia After Natural Gas Cuts
item.description: Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is scheduled to meet his Indonesian counterpart in Jakarta on Tuesday, days after Indonesia trimmed natural gas exports to the city-state.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Toronto Reelects Chow as Mayor on Affordability Pledges
item.description: Toronto reelected its progressive mayor, Olivia Chow, for a second term on Monday, opting to stick with her agenda of stronger social services and improved affordability.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Shin and Monique Mulima

item.title: Trump Rallies in Mississippi With Republican Senate Seat at Risk
item.description: President Donald Trump urged Republican voters to head to the polls during a campaign rally in deep-red Mississippi, saying he couldn’t “take a chance” of Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith losing her seat.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Bolsonaro Backs Off Election Challenge as His Party Concedes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro abandoned plans to challenge the result of Brazil’s presidential election, while his Liberal Party went a step further and formally conceded defeat to reelected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho

item.title: New DOJ Charges Against Ex-FBI Chief Comey Unsealed by Court
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Keisha Lance Bottoms, Georgia's Democratic gubernatorial candidate, in a pre-recorded interview, says she wants to pause new data center construction while the state examines the industry's impact on the electric grid, consumer costs, public health and water supplies. Mark Esper, former Defense Secretary and Partner at Red Cell Ventures, says he does not see the benefit of a US attack on Iran and says the economic blockade is working. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Bid for Fast Ruling in California Voting Case Rejected
item.description: The Trump administration on Monday struck out in its attempt to rapidly block California from counting 20,000 mail-in ballots from people it says are “likely” non-citizens, though the fight may still be far from over.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Former Rio Tinto Executive to Head Australia’s Weapons Buys
item.description: Australia will appoint the former head of mining giant Rio Tinto Plc’s local operations to run weapons procurement, tapping private-sector experience in complex projects as the country manages a major military buildup.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger
